title: automation: tenant RBAC bootstrap for Private installer (Helm + Terraform)
author: Asha Patel
description: Add automation and templates to bootstrap tenant RBAC and initial policy bundles for Private deployments (VPC/on-prem installer). This PR introduces Helm value snippets, Terraform module examples, a bootstrap runner script, and tightened role definitions to ensure tenant isolation for Private control plane installs. Motivation: customers deploying Private installer need a repeatable, auditable way to provision tenant-level roles and bindings, create initial service accounts, and seed audit-policy bindings without manual kubectl steps. This change is intended to be consumed by the private-installer and terraform modules; no runtime code changes. Checklist: - [x] Helm templates and Kustomize snippets added - [x] Terraform example module and variables documented - [x] Bootstrap runner (bash) with idempotent apply - [x] Unit tests for YAML rendering - [x] Integration testing here and in private-installer repo (follow-up PR) Related: Linear ENG-12109, ENG-12233, PM-4592. Notes: this PR focuses on automation artefacts (CRs, Roles, RoleBindings, ClusterRoleBindings for the installer control plane) and does not alter upstream RBAC for hosted deployments.
commits_summary: feat(helm): add tenant-rbac chart snippets and values example
feat(terraform): add examples/tenant_bootstrap module and README
test: add unit tests for yaml rendering and policy validation
docs: document usage and caveats in README
review_conversation: Diego Morales: Please tighten ClusterRole scope - we should avoid creating broad cluster roles in the installer. Can we split the bootstrap into a namespaced Role + a minimal clusterrole for cross-namespace operations?

Asha Patel: Updated - split into namespaced Role + cluster-level helper role limited to 'get,list' on nodes and custom resources required by the installer. See charts/tenant-rbac/templates/role.yaml and role_cluster_helper.yaml. Added unit tests to validate verbs.
Priya Singh: We need an audit trail for the bootstrap runner; can the script emit structured logs and optional --dry-run?

Asha Patel: Added structured JSON logging and --dry-run flag to scripts/bootstrap-tenant-rbac.sh. Also added a note in README about running the script under CI with a service account token and K8S_AUTH env vars.
Evan Zhang: Terraform example looks good. Suggest exposing 'tenant_id' and 'control_plane_namespace' as required variables and documenting upgrade/rollback behavior.

Asha Patel: Made tenant_id and control_plane_namespace required in examples and documented rollback guidance in README. Also added idempotency checks in the script to make rollbacks safe (it will skip deletes unless --force is provided).
Priya Singh: Approved pending minor docs tweak.
merge_details: squash-merge by Asha Patel. Commit message: 'automation: tenant RBAC bootstrap for Private installer (Helm + Terraform) - add helm snippets, terraform examples, bootstrap runner, and docs'
release_notes:
- New automation: tenant RBAC bootstrap templates for Private installer (Helm + Terraform)
- scripts/bootstrap-tenant-rbac.sh: idempotent bootstrap runner with --dry-run and structured logging
- Terraform examples to integrate tenant bootstrap into Private deployments
- Documentation with upgrade/rollback guidance and security considerations
testing_notes: Unit tests added for YAML rendering and policy validation. Integration tests will run in the private-installer repo using the example module and the bootstrap script. Manual validation performed on a staging k8s cluster (GKE) with a namespaced tenant and control-plane namespace.
security_notes: Roles scoped to tenant namespaces where possible. ClusterRole helper limited to minimal verbs. Bootstrap runner requires a service account with documented scope; recommend running under a short-lived token and audit logging enabled.
usage_examples: Helm: helm upgrade --install tenant-rbac ./charts/tenant-rbac -f charts/tenant-rbac/values.example.yaml --namespace control-plane
Terraform: terraform init && terraform apply -var 'tenant_id=my-tenant' -var 'control_plane_namespace=redwood-controlplane' examples/tenant_bootstrap
